summary: Looks up a driver name string (read from a per-driver record in a global table) and maps it to a numeric driver ID chosen from a fixed table, gated by the name-category index a3, the boolean a4 and the flag a5. On a successful match it copies a global buffer, writes the matched ID to a1+8, the secondary value from ShortComputation_41a0 to a1+12, clears the byte at a1+16, and returns 0; otherwise it returns 1 without touching the outputs. Called by sub_414600 (0x00414600).

local_names.a1: output struct base: matched driver ID written at +8, secondary value at +12, zero flag byte at +16
local_names.a2: driver-record index used to locate the name field via dword_8AC394 + 1060 * a2 + 188
local_names.a3: name-category index: 0 selects one pair of comparison tables, 1 selects another; other values fall through unmatched
local_names.a4: boolean selecting between two ID columns inside each driver's table entry
local_names.a5: boolean selecting between the two name-table variants within a category
local_names.v5: matched driver numeric ID (defaults to -1 and is only committed when greater than 0)
local_names.v6: secondary value returned by ShortComputation_41a0(a3), also used as a success gate

operations.description: Compute the secondary value v6 = ShortComputation_41a0(a3) from the name-category index a3 before any lookup.
If v6 < 0 the function returns 1 immediately, treating the category index as invalid.
The record lookup proceeds only when the driver-record index a2 >= 0.
Compute v7 = dword_8AC394 + 1060 * a2 to index into a fixed-stride per-driver record table, then v8 = v7 + 188 as the address of the record's name string.
Continue only when the computed record pointer v7 is nonzero; otherwise fall through to the failure path.

When a3 == 1 and a5 is set, compare the name at v8 via sub_566810(v8, <driver-name-global>) against MichaelS, RubensB, MikaH, DavidC, RalfS, Juan, HeinzHaraldF, JarnoT, RicardoZ, JacquesV, OlivierP, EddieI, PedroDe, NickH, KimiR, JeanA, LucianoB, GastonM, JosV, EnriqueB, GiancarloF, JensonB, FernandoA, TarsoM, AllanM, AlexY, FelipeM, MikaS, ThomasE, TakumaS, MarkW, AlexanderW, AlessandroZana, DamonH, JohnnyH, LucaB, MarcG, PedroDi and ToranosukeT to select the numeric ID.
When a3 == 1 and a5 is clear, run the same sub_566810(v8, <driver-name-global>) comparison chain against the same 39 driver-name globals with the alternative ID column.
When a3 == 0 and a5 is set, run the same sub_566810(v8, <driver-name-global>) comparison chain against the same 39 driver-name globals with the a3==0 ID column.
When a3 == 0 and a5 is clear, run the same sub_566810(v8, <driver-name-global>) comparison chain against the same 39 driver-name globals with the final a3==0 ID column.
A matched driver name selects its numeric ID from the a4-nonzero or a4-zero column; comparison chains that assign only a tail register (v9) resolve v5 = v9 at the LABEL_321 merge point.
On a successful lookup, copy the global name buffer via StringCopyWithBufferRealloc(&byte_5EA438).
Commit the outputs on the a1 output struct: *(a1 + 8) = v5 (matched driver ID), *(a1 + 12) = v6 (secondary value), *(a1 + 16) = 0 (success flag byte).
Return 0 (success) only when v6 > 0 and v5 > 0; every other path returns 1.
This lookup is invoked by sub_414600 (0x00414600), which consumes the driver ID / secondary value written into a1.
